5.headline: The week the data turned out to be wrong
shots: 4am, head torch on, dark empty street. Hold it 5 seconds, say nothing. This is the signature image of the series.
Rolling power blocks: phone on a fence post, run through frame twice. 15s.
Screen record: tap between Outside and Treadmill on a session so the one-line brief swaps. Shows the app doing something real.
Screen record: the heart rate block, then open 'Why ~?'. This is the honesty angle on camera.
Garage: start the treadmill, let the mic catch the noise, close the door and walk out. No dialogue needed.
Garmin sleep screen showing the 7:59pm bed time. Point at it.
The course elevation profile on screen, your finger landing on kilometre 6.
Piece to camera, post-run: 'my coach was wrong about four things this week and told me every time.'
The steep hill from the bottom, before the first rep. Phone low, looking up it.
The top of the hill looking back down the 205m line, first light. The whole session is this, four times.
talk: For five weeks the plan was built around a course nobody had looked at. The official KML was on the race website the whole time.
Kilometre 6 is 800 metres at 9.8%. It has cost roughly the same two and a half minutes in every race, and it is the only kilometre that did not improve last year.
My max heart rate was set to 190. In the 2024 race I averaged 198 for a full kilometre. Every training zone I have used was built on a number about ten beats too low.
The garage treadmill is too loud at 4am. That one domestic fact restructured 22 weeks of training.
Two weekend slots means the belt is now the most race-specific session I own, because nothing outdoors near me does 800 metres at 10%.
The trail was a 30 minute drive I could not make, so the session got better instead of worse: the hill five minutes away is closer to the climb that actually decides this race than the trail is.
I had told him nothing near home could replicate the climb. Then he pointed out the big hill five minutes from his door. That is the second thing this week I asserted without checking.
The hill is 17 metres. The race climb is 78. That is not a failure of the hill, it is the reason the session had to change shape.
log: Course measured, finally

Parsed the organiser's official KML: 10.04km, 255m gain smoothed against their 294m raw. One decisive climb of 800m at 9.8% from the 4.6km mark, a third of the total gain in one hit. 20% of the course descends at -5% or steeper, 750m of it steeper than -10%.
Found the real 2024 race

It was on Strava titled 'First ever trail event. 10km', not 'Beerwah'. 1:08:14 elapsed, matching the official 1:08:31. The climb sat at kilometre 8 that year, so the course layout did change after February 2024. Confirmed what you remembered.
Max HR 190 to 200, threshold 172 to 182

Set off three years of race files. You averaged 198bpm for a full kilometre climbing in 2024 and spent 51 minutes above 181. All 39 activities in intervals.icu recalculated against the corrected zones.
Easy ceiling moved from 148 to 158
Direct consequence of the threshold correction. The early-block 'drifting too fast on easy runs' problem was partly a bad number, not bad discipline.
Climbing came off the weekdays
4am terrain tops out at 5-6% for thirty seconds. All climbing moved to a dedicated weekend treadmill session that can actually hold 10-12%. Thursday is now flat aerobic volume.
Weekend split into two sessions
TRAIL DAY outdoors for footing and descents, TREADMILL CLIMB for the km 6 rehearsal. Either day, your call.
Night work solved
From late November the weekend trail day runs in the dark with a head torch, instead of a weekday session that was never going to happen.
Four unverified claims deleted
'The Dungeon', the 10.4km distance, 'the final 3km is mostly uphill', and 'sustained climbing not short bursts' were all invented rather than sourced. Removed from the plan and the race-day card.
Weekend swapped, hill in front of trail

Sat 29 Aug: the trail is a 30 minute drive and the drive was not on, so the trail moved to Sunday and a steep hill five minutes from home took Saturday. That is an upgrade, not a fallback. The KML says Beerwah is decided by one climb, 800m at 9.8% from the 4.6km mark. The rolling route is 5-6% and gets run twice midweek already. A long steep hill is the closest thing available to km 6, so the km 6 session arrived a week early and outdoors: 3 x 3 min uphill, walk down, full recovery. Three reps not four, because the hill is unmeasured and the right hamstring spoke up on Thursday. Sunday's trail is gated on that hamstring, because descending is what turns tight into torn and this race is 20% descent.
Stale heart rate numbers cleaned out of 36 sessions

The zone change on 26 Aug updated the heart rate box on every session but not the older prescription text underneath it, so 35 sessions were telling him under 158 in one panel and under 148 in the next. All of them now read off the current threshold of 182.
Routes named, and the treadmill lost its monopoly

He mapped his ground: north from the house is rolling hills, south is flat and easy, and Point Cartwright five minutes away is the big hill. Every session in the plan now names where to run it. The rule is flat for anything judged on pace, rolling for strength, the big hill for the climb that decides the race, the trail for descents. The bigger change: the km 6 session was built as a treadmill session on the claim that nothing outdoors nearby replicates 800m at 10%. That claim was mine and it was never checked. Point Cartwright exists. All 20 of those sessions are now 'CLIMB SESSION' rather than 'TREADMILL CLIMB', with the hill first and the belt as the wet-weather fallback. The hill is still unmeasured, and the plan says so rather than guessing.
Rules tab was still showing July's zones

The zone table on the Rules tab had never been updated after the 26 Aug recalibration. It was telling him easy meant under 138. It now reads off threshold 182 like everything else, and a routes card sits above it.
Point Cartwright measured, and it is a quarter of the race climb

First run on the hill, 29 Aug. The file says it climbs 9m to 26m: 17m of rise, 205m long at about 8%, 65 seconds. There is a steeper direct line too, 117m at 14.7%, which is the one he took on rep 1 before settling on the longer line for reps 2 to 4. So the gradient is honest and close to the race's 9.8%. The length is not. Beerwah's decisive climb is 800m at 9.8%, five to seven minutes, 78m of rise, which is four and a half of these laps end to end. The session gave 4 minutes 20 of climbing where the race asks for one unbroken block of five to seven.
Climb sessions rebuilt around laps

Weeks 6 to 12 now run at Cartwright as continuous laps: up the 205m line, jog straight back down, no stopping, three or four laps to a block. The climbing adds up to the length the race wants and the jogged descents cover the 20% of Beerwah that descends, which is the part never trained. Weeks 13 and beyond stay on the belt for now, because a 6 minute block is six laps back to back and a 12 minute block is eleven, and at that point it is a fartlek, not a climb. Week 6's warm-up has one job: measure the longer ocean-footpath approach and settle that question with a file.
